raw_response:
I’m farming 66 mu this year, and I’m not going to spread myself too thin. The wheat is already in the ground from last October, so at this point I mainly need to carry it safely to harvest, then turn those same fields quickly into summer maize. That wheat-maize rotation is still my main steady income, so I’ll keep **40 mu** in that double-crop system. On the other **26 mu**, I’ll split between **14 mu stevia** and **12 mu sweet potato**. Stevia can bring better cash if the stand is good, but it needs more attention and labor. Sweet potato is steadier and doesn’t scare me as much in a bad year.

With my middle-school education, I do listen when the extension people talk about split fertilizer and timing, but I still mostly go by what I’ve seen on my own land and what nearby farmers are doing. Wheat cannot be starved now, especially if I want a decent harvest in June, so I’ll give it one more nitrogen topdress and two irrigations if the weather stays dry. For maize after wheat, I won’t chase an extreme yield target, but I also won’t cut fertilizer too much because underfeeding maize usually shows up fast. Stevia and sweet potato I’ll manage more carefully on area, not too much acreage, because they take more hands and cash. I’d rather keep the plan balanced than gamble everything on one crop.
